Adverse childhood experiences (simulated)

aces.Rd

Retrospective reports of eight adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) by 1,500 adults, with covariates, a sampling weight and three adult health outcomes. Designed for latent class analysis (lca()), multigroup LCA by sex, one-step covariates, r3step(), bch(), dcat() and sampling weights.

Usage

aces

Format

A data frame with 1,500 rows and 16 columns:

id

Respondent id.

ace_emo_abuse

Emotional abuse before age 18 (0/1).

ace_phys_abuse

Physical abuse (0/1).

ace_sex_abuse

Sexual abuse (0/1).

ace_emo_neglect

Emotional neglect (0/1).

ace_phys_neglect

Physical neglect (0/1).

ace_violence

Witnessed domestic violence (0/1).

ace_substance

Household substance misuse (0/1).

ace_mental

Household mental illness (0/1).

female

1 = woman.

age

Age in years, 18–64.

low_parent_edu

Neither parent had post-secondary education (0/1); oversampled.

weight

Sampling weight (mean 1) undoing the oversampling.

depress

Depressive symptoms, CES-D-8 style sum score, 0–24.

srh

Self-rated health: 1 excellent, 2 very good, 3 good, 4 fair, 5 poor.

smoker

Current smoker (0/1).

Each ACE item is missing completely at random with probability 0.02, depress with 0.04.

Source

Simulated (no real person is described) by datasets/generate.jl of the Julia package LatentMixtures.jl (seed Xoshiro(20261101)); full codebook in its datasets/README.md. Data generating process: four classes, Low adversity, Household dysfunction, Maltreatment, High adversity (sample shares 0.523, 0.199, 0.167, 0.111; weighted 0.548, 0.188, 0.163, 0.101), with P(item = 1 | class) for emotional abuse .05/.20/.75/.85, physical abuse .03/.12/.60/.75, sexual abuse .02/.05/.25/.40 (men; +0.9 on the logit scale for women in every class, i.e. measurement non-invariance by sex), emotional neglect .04/.15/.65/.80, physical neglect .02/.08/.30/.55, domestic violence .03/.50/.15/.80, household substance .05/.65/.15/.85, household mental illness .06/.50/.20/.75. Class membership is a multinomial logit on low_parent_edu, female and age. The distal outcomes depend on the class only (plus sex for depress), as BCH and DCAT assume: mean depress 4, 7, 9, 13 (+1 for women); P(smoker) .15, .28, .25, .40; srh shifts towards poor health with adversity. Modelled on latent class studies of ACEs (Felitti et al. 1998, doi:10.1016/S0749-3797(98)00017-8 ; Shin, McDonald & Conley 2018, Addictive Behaviors 78, 187–192, doi:10.1016/j.addbeh.2017.11.020 ). Licence: CC0 1.0 (public domain).

Raw survey or Mplus files often code missing values as -999; convert them first, e.g. dat[dat == -999] <- NA.

Examples

data(aces)
# eight binary ACE items: how common is each adversity?
round(colMeans(aces[, 2:9], na.rm = TRUE), 3)
#>    ace_emo_abuse   ace_phys_abuse    ace_sex_abuse  ace_emo_neglect 
#>            0.293            0.227            0.151            0.239 
#> ace_phys_neglect     ace_violence    ace_substance       ace_mental 
#>            0.132            0.228            0.283            0.261 
# \donttest{
# which patterns of childhood adversity are there? (4 classes in the generating model)
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)
#> Starting Julia ...
#> Package "Tables.jl" (version >= 1.0) is required. Installing ...
#> Starting Julia ...
classprobs(m)   # close to the generating shares 0.52, 0.20, 0.17, 0.11
#> [1] 0.56010023 0.18552219 0.15563946 0.09873811
# }
